description: Fig. 9 is a two-panel composite of polar (planar-projection) contour plots giving the directional dependence of the Young's modulus E (GPa) calculated for the Fe1−xMnxAl system; no micrographs are present. Panel (a) is the projection on the (001) crystallographic plane, horizontal axis labelled [100] E/GPa with ticks from −400 to 400 in steps of 100, vertical axis labelled [010] E/GPa with ticks ±100, ±200, ±300, ±400. Panel (b) is the projection on the (110) plane, horizontal axis [1-10] E/GPa with ticks −600 to 600 (step 200), vertical axis [001] E/GPa with ticks ±100 to ±400, the outer contour extending past the highest legible tick. Both panels share the same dashed-line legend of nine compositions: FeAl, Fe0.875Mn0.125Al, Fe0.75Mn0.25Al, Fe0.625Mn0.375Al, Fe0.5Mn0.5Al, Fe0.375Mn0.625Al, Fe0.25Mn0.75Al, Fe0.125Mn0.875Al and MnAl. Each composition draws one closed, clearly non-circular (rounded-square/lobed) contour; the largest contour reaches roughly ±300–400 GPa on (a) and ~±600 GPa along [1-10] on (b), while the remaining contours cluster within about ±200 GPa and intersect one another in (b). The strongly non-spherical shapes demonstrate pronounced Young's-modulus anisotropy on both planes; no modulus value is printed on any curve, only axis ticks.

subfigures.description: Polar projection of Young's modulus on the (001) plane: horizontal axis [100] E/GPa (−400 to 400, step 100), vertical axis [010] E/GPa (±100–±400). Nine dashed closed contours, one per Fe1−xMnxAl composition; the outermost contour reaches about ±300 to ±400 GPa at the diagonal corners, while the remaining contours are clustered within roughly ±200 GPa, giving a lobed, non-circular shape. Legend listed at the right in two blocks (FeAl … Fe0.5Mn0.5Al, then Fe0.375Mn0.625Al … MnAl).

Polar projection of Young's modulus on the (110) plane: horizontal axis [1-10] E/GPa (−600 to 600, step 200), vertical axis [001] E/GPa (±100–±400, outer contour beyond the top tick). Nine dashed contours as in (a); the largest spans roughly ±600 GPa along [1-10], and the smaller contours cross one another to form a bow-tie/cross-like pattern, so the composition ranking of E reverses between the [001] and [1-10] directions.

observations.observation: Fig. 9 consists of two side-by-side polar contour panels, labelled (001) on the left and (110) on the right, both plotting Young's modulus E in GPa against crystallographic direction.
Panel (a) horizontal axis is labelled [100] E/GPa with ticks from −400 to 400 in steps of 100; the vertical axis is labelled [010] E/GPa with ticks at ±100, ±200, ±300 and ±400.
Panel (b) horizontal axis is labelled [1-10] E/GPa with ticks from −600 to 600 in steps of 200; the vertical axis is labelled [001] E/GPa with ticks at ±100, ±200, ±300 and ±400.

Both panels carry the same dashed-line legend of nine compositions: FeAl, Fe0.875Mn0.125Al, Fe0.75Mn0.25Al, Fe0.625Mn0.375Al, Fe0.5Mn0.5Al, Fe0.375Mn0.625Al, Fe0.25Mn0.75Al, Fe0.125Mn0.875Al and MnAl, split into two legend blocks.

Every contour in both panels is strongly non-circular (lobed/rounded-square), and the contours within one panel do not nest concentrically — they intersect each other, which indicates that the ranking of E among the alloys depends on crystallographic direction.

In panel (a) the single outermost contour reaches roughly the ±300 to ±400 GPa level near the corners while the remaining contours are confined to about ±200 GPa; in panel (b) the outermost contour reaches about ±600 GPa along [1-10]. No numeric modulus values are printed on the curves themselves.
The figure caption states that Fig. 9 shows planar projections of Young's modulus of the Fe1−xMnxAl system on (001) and (110) crystallographic planes.
The citing text states that on the (001) and (110) planes the Young's modulus has a strong directional dependence.
The citing text states that at the [100], [010], [001] and [110] directions Fe0.125Mn0.875Al shows the maximum Young's modulus and MnAl the minimum Young's modulus.
The citing text states that the planar contours of these alloys on the (001) and (110) planes are not close to a spherical shape, indicating strong Young's-modulus anisotropy on these planes.
